hosting.//: The marketing site, which also serves the two PUBLIC pages an owner shares: a profile and a show. cleanUrls drops the .html from every page (/profile.html is served at /profile and 301s to it) because a link people paste into a message should not carry a file extension. The rewrites put the thing the page is ABOUT in the path — /profile/<slug> and /event/<id> — and the page reads that last segment itself (readSlug / readEventId). Both pages still accept the older ?slug= / ?event= query forms, so links already out in the world keep working.

headers.//: Catch-all so the bare root is covered too: `*.html` misses `/` (a directory index), which is why the root served max-age=3600 while /index.html did not. Also covers the unhashed scene scripts, whose URLs are stable so a fix would otherwise sit behind a cache.
Re-asserted AFTER the catch-all (last match wins): Vite's bundle is content-hashed, so the filename changes whenever the content does.

hosting.//: The React SPA. Every path must serve index.html so TanStack Router owns routing; the hashed Vite bundle is immutable, so it caches hard while the shell revalidates.

headers.//: Catch-all: every non-asset path serves the SPA shell (via the rewrite), and a cached shell points at asset hashes that no longer exist after a deploy. COOP is same-origin-allow-popups because Firebase Auth's signInWithPopup polls window.closed on the popup — the stricter default blocks that and the flow can hang when a user dismisses the popup by hand.
Re-asserted AFTER the catch-all so it wins for the content-hashed bundle, whose filename changes whenever its content does.
